output.brief:
The rise in VA-220 failures traces to Pellacott's 2026-built valves, not to the new installers or firmware 4.2. Brenmoor's lab matched claims to valve source, installer and firmware. Pellacott valves fail at about 41 per 1,000 units whichever installer or firmware is involved. Durrant-Hale valves stay at 5–7. Teardowns show a deformed, unseated slide seal. Untouched warehouse valves from Pellacott's 2026 lots leak at the seat 11% of the time, against 0–1% for older Pellacott lots and Durrant-Hale valves. The independent calibration visit found Pellacott's leak-test rig out of service since January 2026. The rig has no VA-220 test program, and the certificate tables repeat four fixed sequences that also appear in November 2025 certificates. The certificates therefore do not appear to record real tests. Pellacott's score rose largely because it began submitting complete-looking records.

Next steps: quarantine 2026-built Pellacott stock, including the six held lots. Do not release them on fresh certificates. Suspend dock-to-stock for Pellacott and run Brenmoor's own helium testing. Shift volume toward Durrant-Hale to limit the line stoppage. Drop the installer chargeback. Require rig logs or witnessed tests in scoring. Check other suppliers' records. The seal-versus-assembly cause is still unresolved, so reverting to Ferrand is premature.
